content.text: Describe editable block data
Attribute specs are how Uncial derives the editing UI you'd otherwise hand-build: each spec maps a component prop to a typed, validated control in the block attributes panel.
default
— Required fallback value. Shorthand values like title: "" become defaults.
input
— Editor control hint: text, textarea, number, checkbox, json, richtext, select, image, or hidden. Left out, it is guessed from the default value.
required
— Marks an attribute as required during validation.
validate
— Custom predicate for accepting or rejecting an attribute value.
parse / serialize
— Coerce values at editor or persistence boundaries.
options
— Allowed values for select-style attributes.
Let authors add images
Give an attribute
input: 'image'
and the attributes panel shows an image field for it. The attribute stores a plain URL string.
Where images come from is up to you. Pass an
imageSource
to
Editor
with any of these three functions, and the field shows a button for each one you provide:
upload(file)
— save the file somewhere and return the URL to store. Adds an Upload button.
browse()
— return the URLs of images that already exist. Adds a Choose existing button that opens a picker.
thumbnail(src)
— turn a stored URL into one the browser can show. Use it when the stored value is not directly displayable, such as an ID or a path without a base.

<script lang="ts">
	import { Editor, type ImageSource } from 'uncial';
	import { blocks, schema, attributesController } from './uncial';

	const imageSource: ImageSource = {
		async upload(file) {
			const body = new FormData();
			body.append('file', file);
			const response = await fetch('/api/images', { method: 'POST', body });
			return (await response.json()).url;
		},
		async browse() {
			return (await fetch('/api/images')).json();
		}
	};

	let document = $state({ type: 'doc', content: [{ type: 'paragraph' }] });
</script>

<Editor {blocks} {schema} {attributesController} {imageSource} bind:json={document} />
Right after an upload, the editor shows the image from a local
blob:
copy, so it appears at once even if your server is slow to serve it. The document still stores the URL that
upload
returned.
On a site built with uncial-cms you do not write an image source:
EditorPage
uses
cmsImageSource
, which commits uploads to your repository. See

Allow nested document flow

Nesting is where form-driven admins fall apart — and where in-place editing pays off most. Editors write nested content inside the rendered block, exactly where it will appear, not in a collapsed sub-form three scroll-screens away.

Atomic blocks have no child content. Add content: { kind: 'flow' } when a block should own one default child region; the block component then receives its attribute props plus a children snippet for that region.

Svelte ships first, core stays neutral

Svelte is the only bundled block runtime today. Non-Svelte block authoring is enabled through public runtime plugins that normalize native components and can provide editor node-view mounting. A registry may contain blocks from only one runtime in this release; mixed-runtime documents fail fast.

Svelte blocks keep the direct Svelte renderer path, so custom block rendering remains SSR-capable. Future React or Vue support should be implemented with full-document runtime renderers that can use each framework's SSR APIs, not by mixing client-only component islands into the Svelte renderer.
